children: By Janet H. Cho
Lululemon Athletica, best known for its yoga clothes and other specialty athleticwear, reported quarterly revenue that fell short of expectations and lowered its full-year guidance.
For its second fiscal quarter ended in July, Lululemon reported sales of $2.4 billion, below the $2.458 billion Wall Street expected, and down from $2.525 billion in the year-ago quarter.
Adjusted earnings of $2.92 a share beat projections for $1.79 a share, but that included 86 cents a share from federal tariff refunds.
Lululemon said it received $134.5 million in refunds during the quarter, plus $4.1 million in interest, which reduced its cost of goods sold and increased its per-share earnings.
Same-store sales fell 9% during the quarter, nearly double the decline of 4.6% that analysts had projected.
Lululemon stock dropped 18% to $99.88 in Friday's premarket.

"While we continue to navigate some challenging dynamics, we are taking a prudent approach with our revised full-year outlook," Interim Co-CEO and Chief Financial Officer Meghan Frank said, adding that "we have confidence in the strength of the lululemon brand, the deep connection we have with our guests and ambassadors, and the significant opportunities we see to drive long-term growth."

Interim co-CEO, President, and Chief Commercial Officer André Maestrin said they were confident in their ability to take the right steps to strengthen their performance. "We look forward to welcoming our incoming CEO, Heidi O'Neill, next week as we begin an exciting new chapter for the company."
Lululemon announced in April that longtime Nike veteran Heidi O'Neill would be its new chief executive, effective Sept. 8.

The specialty athleticwear, footwear, and accessories company said its quarterly revenue drop was primarily related to an 8% drop in revenue in the Americas. That was partly offset by a 4% climb in revenue in mainland China and the rest of the world.
It added nine net new company-operated stores during the quarter, ending with 825 stores.
For the current third quarter, Lululemon expects revenue of $2.29 billion to $2.32 billion, a decline of 10% to 11% from a year ago. It expects adjusted earnings of 93 cents to 98 cents a share.

For its full fiscal year ending in January 2027, Lululemon forecasts sales of $10.35 billion to $10.5 billion, which would be 5% to 7% lower than the year before. That's down from its earlier guidance of $11 billion to $11.15 billion in revenue and earnings of $10.95 to $11.15 a share.
It guided for adjusted full-year earnings of $9.48 to $9.73 a share, including the 86 cents a share from second-quarter tariff refunds, but does not expect any more refunds.
Analysts were expecting full-year sales of $11.03 billion and adjusted earnings of $10.84 a share, according to FactSet.
It expects to add 35 net new stores this fiscal year, down from previous guidance for 40 net new stores.
The stock is down 41.4% this year through Thursday's close and down 40.9% over the past 12 months, before its latest financial results were reported.
